text: So the rain gauge is pretty simple. Rain falls into a funnel and then into a cylinder. The top of the funnel is much bigger than the tube below. So if it is ten times the area, then an inch of rain will fill the tube up to ten inches. This magnification allows you to read it very easily and precisely. You can measure hundredths of an inch. But rain gauges are subject to some errors. One is evaporation. The rain that collects in the gauge can evaporate quickly, especially in warm or windy weather. Another is wind exposure. If there is a lot of wind blowing, it creates turbulence around the mouth of the gauge. And that can carry rain drops over the mouth, and so it will underestimate the rainfall.
